Meet Corliss Archer
A program from radio's Golden Age that ran from January 7, 1943 to September 30, 1956; it was CBS's answer to NBC's popular A Date with Judy, was broadcast by NBC in 1948 as a summer replacement for The Bob Hope Show, aired on ABC from October 3, 1952 to June 26, 1953, then returned to CBS; fewer than 24 episodes are known to exist.
American television sitcom that aired on CBS from July 13, 1951 to August 10, 1951 and in syndication via the Ziv Company from April to December 1954; it was an adaptation of the radio series of the same name.

Suffrajett
Suffrajett is a United States rock band from New York City, currently based in Chicago, Illinois, composed of singer/violinist Simi Sernaker, guitarist Jason Chasko, bassist Kevin Roberts, and drummer Danny Severson. It has toured with Local H, The Last Vegas, Bob Schneider, Juliette and the Licks, and Scissors for Lefty, opened for MC5, and released a self-titled debut album on February 2, 2003 and Black Glitter on January 1, 2007.

An Afro-Boricua teenager living in Brooklyn; granddaughter of a shadowshaper; must learn about her artistic and spiritual heritage to foil the killer.

2006–07 QMJHL season
The 38th season in the history of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League; its regular season ran from September 14, 2006 to March 18, 2007.

Quebec Major Junior Hockey League
The league whose 38th season was the 2006–07 QMJHL season.

regular season
The 2006–07 QMJHL regular season ran from September 14, 2006 to March 18, 2007; eighteen teams played 70 games each in the schedule.

Lewiston Maineiacs
Finished first overall in the 2006–07 QMJHL regular season, winning their first Jean Rougeau Trophy; won 16 playoff games while losing only one en route to their first President's Cup, defeating the Val-d'Or Foreurs in the finals.

Jean Rougeau Trophy
Award won by the Lewiston Maineiacs for finishing first overall in the 2006–07 regular season; it was their first.

President's Cup
Trophy won by the Lewiston Maineiacs, their first, after they defeated the Val-d'Or Foreurs in the finals.

Val-d'Or Foreurs

Wilford H. Fawcett House
House in Breezy Point, Minnesota, United States, listed on the National Register of Historic Places; also referred to as the Fawcett House, built by Wilford H. Fawcett as a private residence within the resort property.

Wilford H. Fawcett
Also known as "Captain Billy"; started Captain Billy's Whiz Bang as a joke book for soldiers during World War I; formed Fawcett Publications in 1919 in Robbinsdale, Minnesota; in 1920 bought land where the present-day Breezy Point Resort is located and began building cottages and a large log lodge; built the Fawcett House as a private residence within the resort property; hired Magney and Tusler and commissioned the design in the Swiss Chateau style.

Captain Billy
Alias for Wilford H. Fawcett.

Captain Billy's Whiz Bang

World War I

Fawcett Publications
Publication company formed by Wilford H. Fawcett in 1919 in Robbinsdale, Minnesota.

Robbinsdale, Minnesota
Location where Wilford H. Fawcett formed Fawcett Publications in 1919.

Breezy Point, Minnesota
Location of the Wilford H. Fawcett House in Minnesota, United States.

National Register of Historic Places
Register on which the Wilford H. Fawcett House is listed.

Breezy Point Resort
Present-day resort located on land Wilford H. Fawcett bought in 1920; the Fawcett House was built as a private residence within the resort property; the local logging industry had declined before the resort was built.

cottages
Cottages Wilford H. Fawcett began building after buying land in 1920.

large log lodge
Large log lodge Wilford H. Fawcett began building after buying land in 1920; it has since burnt down.

Magney and Tusler
Minneapolis architects hired by Wilford H. Fawcett; Fawcett commissioned the design in the Swiss Chateau style.

Minneapolis
City of the architects Magney and Tusler.

Swiss Chateau style
Architectural style in which Wilford H. Fawcett commissioned the design.

logging industry

Square Enix companion books
Dozens of companion books have been produced since 1998; they focus on artwork, developer interviews, and background information on the fictional worlds and characters in games rather than on gameplay details. Square Enix resumed publication of them.

Square
Video game developer that began producing companion books in 1998 and merged with video game publisher Enix on April 1, 2003 to form Square Enix.

Perfect Works
The first series of companion books, written and published by Square subsidiary DigiCube; three books were produced between 1998 and 1999 before the line was stopped in favor of Ultimania.

DigiCube
Square subsidiary that wrote and published Perfect Works and published the Ultimania series until it was dissolved in 2003.

Ultimania
Companion book series, a portmanteau of ultimate and mania (アルティマニア, Arutimania), written by Studio BentStuff and published by DigiCube until 2003.

Studio BentStuff
Writer of the Ultimania series; had previously written game guides for Square for Final Fantasy VII.

Final Fantasy VII
Game for which Studio BentStuff had previously written game guides for Square.

Enix
Video game publisher that merged with Square on April 1, 2003 to form Square Enix.

Square Enix
Company formed by the merger of Square and Enix on April 1, 2003; it resumed publication of the companion books.
